Lessons.Title: Looking at Rates of Change
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: compute average rate of change of exponential functions over specified intervals and explain why the same model has different secant slopes depending on interval. Independent Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 5 Lesson 10, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/5/10/preparation.html and student tasks https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/5/10/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The source revisits solar-cost and coffee-shop changes, emphasizing finite differences per time.

Original fictional account model F(t)=10·2^t tokens for whole days t≥0 gives F0=10,F1=20,F2=40,F3=80. Average rate from day0 to1 is (20−10)/1=10 tokens/day; from day1 to2 is (40−20)/1=20 tokens/day; from day0 to3 is (80−10)/3=70/3≈23.33 tokens/day.

An exponential function has a constant multiplicative factor, not a constant additive per-unit rate. A secant line based on the full interval 0–3 captures a net average; it does not describe each individual step. Predictions that extend a short-period rate linearly may therefore be wrong: day1's rate10 cannot forecast day3 as40 when actual model gives80.

Student task: choose two different intervals, draw corresponding secant slopes over one exponential graph, interpret their units and compare short versus long interval predictions. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 each for endpoint read, quotient arithmetic, model-appropriate rate interpretation and explicit limitation of linear prediction.

KeyConcepts.Title: Secant average rate
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use endpoint outputs and time difference.

KeyConcepts.Title: Nonconstant exponential difference
KeyConcepts.Definition: Equal-time ratios may be equal while equal-time differences change.

KeyConcepts.Title: Prediction limitation
KeyConcepts.Definition: A single secant slope need not hold for other intervals on a nonlinear curve.
KeyConcepts.Example: Linear extension from day1 underestimates day3.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Reporting the multiplicative factor as average rate
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Factor2 is dimensionless, rate has tokens/day units.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assuming all exponential secant slopes equal
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Successive differences change even when ratio is constant.

SummaryPoints: Exponential functions have changing additive rates of change.
Secant slope must name a particular interval and units.
A constant multiplier does not imply a constant derivative or secant rate.
